decisions.fork: F1 Intervention: forecast construction and horizon
decisions.decision:
Forecast: causal, anchored and one-sided.
- Profile: m(b) is the mean of the absolute 15-min measured factor profiles (v13.forecast_profile, the existing mean aggregator, held from bin 8 as the world holds it) over PRIOR same-kind days.
- 15/11 is excluded a priori as a documented incident day.
- The policy is active only with at least 2 such days: 14/11 <- {12,13}; 15/11 and 16/11 <- {12,13,14}; the snow cells (15/11 pm) <- {12,13,14}. It is off on 17/11 and 18/11.
- Anchoring: on the current measured bin level; other days supply only the growth shape.

PRIMARY instrument: a promise-layer display. Every pickup/drop promise and every revision, published at t with Runner ETA p, is shown as D = max(p, S(t, p - t)). S is promise_stretch.stretch with forecast_weight: g = 1 in the current bin and m(b)/m(b0) in later bins. No H is needed, because each rider's own horizon is integrated.

SECONDARY instrument: closed loop with v1.3 UNCHANGED (forecast-v1), K = 2 (H = 30 min at per-bin refresh), same causal-no15 source lists.
- K is fixed a priori: K = 1 is identically 1 (verified, ratio() line 86-87). For the ~727-s median dev horizon promised at a uniformly random point in a bin, r ≈ 1 + ½(g-1).
- No floor code: causal K=2 r < 1 occurs only in w08 bin 5 (min 0.9882), which is disclosed.

Nothing is tuned on test. Zero-run sensitivities (not decision rules): LOO-no15; 15/11 included; 12/11 excluded (14/11 then has 1 source day and is reported as inactive); two-sided display; crude per-bin stretch.
decisions.rationale:
Within a bin the true path is flat, so the per-rider stretch is the exact time-dependent ETA. Verified on validate-stretch-2026-10-06.txt: 658/660 dev riders with dispatch part 0 have |A - true stretch| ≤ 1.00 s.

Dev evidence (task-B, verified by me read-only, unsaved):
- On the cell where both instruments exist, the display dominates the closed loop: v1.3 visible60 rose 0.080 -> 0.224 and served fell 87 -> 85 (smoke-breakdown-2026-10-06.txt).
- C-30 with LOO-no15 sources: cell-mean late60 7.25% -> 0.00%, visible60 8.78% -> 0.43%, extension 21.2 s.
- Causal pool: 2.57%, because 12/11 has no history.

The causal pool removes the leakage objection. Input-only r-tables (computed this session) show causal-no15 K=2 tracks the true weekday-morning growth: 14/11 w07 bin1 1.057 vs true 1.081; 16/11 1.065 vs 1.041. Excluding 15/11 follows the regulatory meaning of 'anticipated' (regular patterns). The floor rests on a priori asymmetric loss (SOURCES: lateness hurts more than earliness helps). The minimum-history rule is a priori: one day is not a profile.

v1.3 is kept for the closed loop because:
- it is tested (23/23 checks, 8/8 mutants);
- forecast-off is decision-identical to v1.2 (718/718), so the T3.8 naive runs can be reused with one clock;
- it is 77-80 MiB per run vs 118-121 MiB for v1.4, and v1.4 also needs fresh naive comparators, since v1.4-naive differs from v1.2 (5 vs 7 late).
decisions.dissent: Methodologist and practitioner (revised): v1.4 (continuous horizon, 300-s snapshot rebuilds, plus a floor) is the more faithful closed-loop instrument. v1.3's per-bin over-inflation is a known artefact that will exaggerate the integration cost and bias the deployment comparison toward the display layer. Skeptic: excluding 15/11 MORNING data has no outcome-free reason, since its morning factor is near normal (1.02-1.06x other weekdays), so 16/11's pool should include it.

decisions.decision:
Zero runs:
- Display replay for all 5 arms (U, C-30, Mplus-30, Mplus-60, V-30) on all 170 T3.8 test runs. C-30 is the confirmatory arm. U gives the {U, C-30} x {naive, display} factorial ('gate and forecast fix different causes'). Mplus-30, Mplus-60 and V-30 are descriptive, including own-break measured against the displayed promise.
- Display replay on task-B dev runs (all arms) and the 15 calibration runs, descriptive and flagged as previews.
- Equal-price pad comparators, computed from promises only: PRIMARY a per-window pad; SENSITIVITY a citywide pad.

New closed-loop runs: C-30F and Mplus-30F only. No U-F, Mplus-60F or V-30F.

Naive comparators: the existing T3.8 C-30 and Mplus-30 runs, reused ONLY if the equivalence controls in F3 pass.

Zero-run statement: Mplus-30 forcing on weekend w08 (0.507 mean, verified), where no forecast exists, is unaffected by construction.
decisions.rationale:
The display layer leaves dispatch untouched, so it is exact, rider-paired on identical served sets, and free for every arm.

Only simulation can answer two questions:
- Is Mplus-30's forcing an artefact of naive promises? Forcing happens inside the gate. Verified from analysis-2026-10-02-jobs.tsv: weekday w07 forced 0.769, w08 0.456, w17 0.038. This tests the thesis's headline 'C never forced, M+ forced 41%'. A hostile examiner will raise it regardless.
- What does integration cost? C-30F answers this, and it also gives the paired C-F vs M+-F (H2a under forecast) comparison.

Excluded arms:
- U: its leftover lateness is dispatch-caused (weekday w17 U 6.76% vs C-30 0%).
- V-30 and Mplus-60: they share the M+ mechanism, and V-30 rider outcomes equal Mplus-30.

The per-window pad is the honest strongest buffer an operator would try ('add x% in the morning'). A citywide pad would be a strawman.
decisions.dissent: Practitioner: Mplus forcing is a thesis-internal relabelling of identical rider behaviour. Weekday w07 A>30 s is 0.393 for C-30 vs 0.390 for Mplus-30, and the two rules take the same actions in 30/34 cells. Mplus-30F should therefore be tier 2, with runs spent instead on a same-clock C-30 v1.4 integration pair and on naive snow runs.

decisions.fork: F3 Cell sets, development, equivalence, snow
decisions.decision:
Display primary population:
- The 21 weekday T3.8 test cells where the policy is active, defined by inputs before any outcome.
- That is 8 day-windows in 3 window strata: w07 {14,15,16}, w08 {14,15,16}, w17 {14,16}.
- Note: 15/11 has no w17 test cells (split-t38-v1.json).
- The 34-cell deployment mean is co-reported; the weekend difference is 0 by construction.

Development: task-B (12-13/11 w07) only, the only day-disjoint set.
- The 15 calibration cells share 12 of 13 test day-windows (ICC of C-30 w07 late60 = 0.917, verified), so they are used for NO choice.
- Every earlier look at them (by all three debaters) is disclosed as a preview.

Closed loop: the 16 weekday w07 and w08 test cells, 6 day-windows.
- Weekday w17 is excluded on input grounds: causal r there is 0.976-1.005, so a one-sided rule would be r = 1, identical to naive.
- Weekends are excluded: no forecast.

Equivalence and gates, run BEFORE any test job:
- S1, Mplus-30F smoke on dev d20181112-s10-r1-w07 with the existing forecast-check-k2.json. Implementation check only; its outcomes are never used.
- E1, Mplus-30 v1.3 forecast-off on one weekday w08 test cell drawn with the sealed seed, ORIGINAL label, new output root.
- E2, C-30 v1.3 forecast-on K = 1 sham (causal-no15 sources) on one weekday w07 test cell drawn with the sealed seed, original label.
- Each is compared with its T3.8 run on: decisions with times, signed v/e/p table, served set, alight times, and frames after stripping run-salted fields.
- Positive control at zero runs: the comparator must flag U vs C-30 on the same cell.
- Any failure halts Family B. Pre-declared fallback: fresh v1.3-off naive comparators for the 8 weekday w07 cells only (16 runs), and Family B is restricted to w07.

Snow: optional tier 4, C-30 naive (v1.3 forecast-off) x all 8 built cells, with display replay. Descriptive and framed as an 'unanticipated ordinary-size ramp' (a negative control), not a stress test.
decisions.rationale:
Day-windows are the units of independent traffic information: ICC 0.92, and the 3 cells of 15/11 w07 have late60 0.227/0.207/0.222. Windows are fixed design strata.

The active-population rule follows from the sealed forecast policy, not from outcomes. Weekend cells, where the policy is off, contribute an exact zero.

Closed-loop cells are where the forecast is non-trivial and where M+ forcing lives.

E1 tests the Mplus gate path and environment stability. RideBound-deadline HEAD is 1ce15e9, dated 2026-09-25, i.e. before T3.8. E2 isolates the snapshot-patch path from the r effect (ms rounding). The existing control-off run already showed 718/718 identical decisions for C-30.

Snow:
- Verified 8/8 cells 'ok with label base' (normalize-snow-2026-10-06.out).
- The world anchors at the window start, so the storm's absolute level is absent.
- The in-window ramp (end ratio 1.403/1.460) is milder than weekday mornings (1.469-1.656), and the causal forecast is flat.
- It therefore adds only a ledger illustration, hence the optional tier.
decisions.dissent: Methodologist: the primary should be the 34-cell zero-filled estimand over 13 day-windows, which blocks any 'chosen windows' charge. Practitioner: naive snow runs belong in tier 1, because they supply the 'unanticipated' half of the accountability ledger that the business case rests on.

decisions.fork: F4 Primary outcomes and decision rules
decisions.decision:
Family A (display, C-30, 21 weekday cells; fixed sequence) is primary. Family B (closed loop, 16 cells) is secondary: one classification chain and one non-inferiority chain, each at alpha 0.025, plus a pre-declared deployment rule.

Inference:
- Interval of record: stratified day-window cluster bootstrap.
- Downgrade checks: leave-one-day-out and cluster-t.
- The cell bootstrap is reported for continuity only.

The full rule is in primaryRule.
decisions.rationale:
Lateness against the first shown drop time is the quantity the Via, delivery and paratransit sources price. Churn is the thesis's own UX metric and was the closed loop's failure mode, so it is a sealed guard.

The display outcome is largely previewed: calibration cells share day-windows, and the predictability table has been seen. Family A is therefore labelled a pre-registered measurement, and its genuinely informative step is A3, information vs an equal-price buffer. Dev evidence for A3 (task-B, unsaved): pad 1.80% vs forecast 0.00%.

Stratified cluster resampling avoids the morning-free resamples that sink an unstratified 13-cluster bootstrap (verified: (10/13)^13 = 0.033 > 0.025). Family B carries the real uncertainty, so it gets a classification for the open M+ question instead of a pass/fail. Price is reported, not gated, because no anchored tolerability threshold exists. Earliness is the only over-quoting gate.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic and methodologist: with only 8 clusters (2-3 per stratum), percentile intervals from a stratified cluster bootstrap are coarse and can be anti-conservative. A per-day-window sign count in EVERY active day-window (not just w07), or a cluster-t interval, should be the decisive criterion rather than a downgrade label.

decisions.decision:
All outcomes are paired, descriptive and use the Family A bootstrap.

(1) Price riders see: first drop and first pickup extension (mean, p50, p90; seconds and % of horizon) by window. The demand effect uses the Lyft elasticity -0.0427 applied to the PICKUP extension only, labelled an extrapolation. Also report the count of displayed pickups beyond request + 600 s, an operational inconsistency because feasibility stays naive.

(2) Accuracy: lateness CDF, signed bias, MAE (comparable to Via's 24.24 s), late30/120/300, early60, late pickup > 60 s.

(3) Displayed stability: visible60 and visible120, jump share, and S_j on the displayed sequence. The T3.8 conformal gamma is recomputed on displayed promises with the same alpha and split. No recalibration runs.

(4) Three-way ledger per late rider against the naive first promise: dispatch part Σ(p - e); anticipated traffic (D0 - P0); unanticipated remainder (A - D0 - dispatch). Cell-level shares map to 49 CFR 37.131(f)(3)(ii) and App. D.

(5) The {U, C-30} x {naive, display} factorial, plus display for Mplus-30, Mplus-60 and V-30.

(6) Closed loop:
- served, wait, ride and door-to-door;
- common-rider late60, forced share, own-break, non-normal count;
- earlier/later revision seconds;
- C-30F vs Mplus-30F served (H2a replication, ±2) and action-sequence agreement;
- r-lines checked against the sealed table.

(7) Sensitivities from F1, plus the citywide pad, an additive pad, and an empirical per-bin pad learned from task-B lateness.

(8) Optional tiers: snow late60/late300, the unanticipated share and the ledger; noise world, the share of the display benefit that survives.

(9) Money ($5 Via, $10 Access-A-Ride): labelled illustrative, shown next to the scale gap (late300 = 0 under the capped rules; field thresholds are 10-15 min).
decisions.rationale: Every gain must sit next to its price in seconds and in riders. The ledger turns the forecast into the 'anticipated' baseline that the regulation refers to. That is the practical tool for a contract manager. The factorial is the operator's 'do I need both?' answer, and it costs zero runs. Recomputing gamma tests whether the T3.8 margin, set by one 07-09 cell, was mostly anticipable traffic.
decisions.dissent: Methodologist: under any forecast the ledger identity's residual (alight - last promise) is no longer zero. Splitting 'unanticipated' from forecast error at execution therefore needs the identity re-verified per rider, or the ledger shares are not interpretable. The skeptic adds that money translations should be omitted entirely given the scale gap.

decisions.decision: Seal predictions PA1-PA9 (display), PB1-PB8 (closed loop), PC1 (controls) and the optional PS1/PN1 exactly as listed in predictions. Make no prediction for the dev smoke outcomes or for Branch selection. Disclose that the display predictions are not blind: test-day forecast error and calibration previews were seen. The closed-loop and optional predictions are the ones that can genuinely fail.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic: the display predictions PA1-PA6 are near-certain given the calibration previews and should carry no evidential weight in the write-up. Practitioner: PB1 has no offline proxy for forcing, so its interval is a guess.

decisions.fork: F7 Threats to validity and mitigations
decisions.decision:
Threats, each with its mitigation:

(1) Near-tautology: a uniform citywide factor on a 96-node OD closure, with world and forecast from the same factor source. Mitigation: frame the result as the measured anticipable share and an upper bound for a time-of-day ratio forecast; report forecast error per day-window; make no real-world effect-size claim; run the optional noise tier.

(2) Previewed test: calibration shares day-windows with test (ICC 0.92), and the predictability table has been seen. Mitigation: Family A labelled 'pre-registered measurement'; dev = task-B only; disclose every pre-seal look, including the debaters' unsaved calibration computations and the input-only r-tables in this ruling.

(3) Thin, odd history: 14/11 rests on 12-13/11; 12/11 is possibly the Veterans Day observance (unverified; its 08:00 factor is 2.797 vs 3.34-3.54); one week only. Mitigation: LOO and 12/11-excluded sensitivities; the claim is conditional on this week.

(4) Few clusters (3 weekday mornings). Mitigation: stratified cluster bootstrap, sign counts, leave-one-day-out and cluster-t downgrades.

(5) Reuse of naive runs across code versions. Mitigation: E1/E2 with a positive control, and the fallback rule.

(6) Static-matrix artefact in the closed loop. Mitigation: closed loop is secondary; churn is reported as a static-matrix integration cost, with v1.4 dev showing partial mitigation (0.167 vs 0.224); no claim that forecasting harms stability in general.

(7) Changed served sets (closed loop). Mitigation: B-C1, common-rider late60.

(8) Display assumptions: riders do not react (no cancellations in the sim); the Runner ledger records Runner promises; pickup feasibility stays naive; dwell is stretched. Mitigation: state all of them; count pickups displayed outside the window; check the oracle residual on test (PA8).

(9) Analyst degrees of freedom: one-sided rule, causal pool, 15/11 exclusion, minimum history, visibleD60 metric. Mitigation: list each in the seal with its a priori reason, run a sensitivity for each, and disclose that they were settled after dev looks.

(10) Snow: completed-trip demand, still 108 requests per cell, absolute level removed, one afternoon, overlapping windows. Mitigation: descriptive only, optional.

(11) Scale gap of 60 s vs 10-15 min penalties. Mitigation: claim ETA reliability, not money.

(12) Volatile disk: C: free was ~57,240 MiB this morning and 65,298 MiB at my check. Mitigation: a per-job live gate against GiB floors, seeded order within tiers, so any truncation leaves a random subset.

(13) Evidence-pack errata: the largest 15-min step per day is 5.1-16.2%, not 10.6-16.2% (verified); the snow cells are 8/8 built.

(14) Number provenance. Mitigation: every dev number is regenerated by saved, hashed scripts before the seal; independent re-analysis agent plus a number-tracing reviewer, as in T3.8.
decisions.rationale: These are the routes by which a hostile examiner would attribute the result to tuning, selection, leakage, artefact or circularity. Each is answered by a pre-declared rule, a zero-run analysis or narrower wording.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic: the noise robustness test should be core, not optional, because it is the only direct answer to the tautology attack. Methodologist: W4 noise parameters are uncalibrated (sigma 0.08, rho 0.7, shockRate 0.02), so any noise result is conditional on an arbitrary magnitude.

decisions.rationale:
After the C-30 gate, the remaining failure is morning-ramp lateness: weekday w07 14.44%, the caps barely help, and it is traffic-caused (contract-split-check). Dev evidence shows a promise-layer forecast removes it, and also displayed churn, at about 21 s on a ~13-min quote, while dispatch is untouched. That maps onto deployed ETA layers and onto the 'anticipated' test in 49 CFR 37.131(f)(3)(ii) and App. D. This is a measured effect plus a tool, with no novelty claim.

Runs are spent only where replay cannot answer. The closed-loop M+ question protects the thesis against its most obvious examiner attack, whichever way it comes out.
decisions.dissent: Skeptic, hostile-examiner view: in this world the display result is a closed-form consequence of the factor files. Its research value is small, and the best use of the remaining ~5 weeks is to write up T3.8/T3.9 now, with only the 32-run M+ question as new evidence.

primaryRule:
FAMILY A (PRIMARY; zero-run display replay; arm C-30)

Population: the 21 weekday T3.8 test cells. These form 8 day-windows in 3 window strata: w07 {14,15,16}/11, w08 {14,15,16}/11, w17 {14,16}/11.

Per served rider r:
- t0 = publishedAtMs of the drop initialPromise; P0 = its p.
- A = simTime of the first passengerAlighted.
- Displayed first drop D0 = max(P0, S(t0, P0 - t0)), where S = promise_stretch.stretch with forecast_weight(m, t0) and m = the causal-no15 profile (14/11 <- 12,13; 15/11 and 16/11 <- 12,13,14). Every later drop revision is displayed the same way at its own publishedAtMs.

Cell metrics:
- Y = share of served riders with A - D0 > 60 s. The naive value Y_n is late_drop60 of t38_rider_experience.py (A - P0 > 60 s).
- E = share of served riders with A - D0 < -60 s.
- Vis = share of promised riders whose Σ|D_i - D_{i-1}| over non-closed drop revisions exceeds 60 s. The naive value is visible60.

Estimand: the unweighted mean over the 21 cells of the per-cell paired differences.

Interval of record: stratified day-window cluster bootstrap.
- Within each stratum, resample its day-windows with replacement, pool their cells, and take the cell mean.
- Combine strata with weights 8/21, 8/21 and 5/21.
- B = 10,000, random.Random(20261007), 95% percentile interval = sorted indices 249 and 9750.

Fixed sequence (each step is tested only if the previous one passes):
- A1 (accuracy): passes iff ALL of:
  - point ΔY ≤ -2.0 pp;
  - UB95(ΔY) < 0;
  - ΔY < 0 in each of the 3 weekday-w07 day-windows;
  - point ΔE ≤ +1.0 pp.
- A2 (churn guard): passes iff UB95(ΔVis) ≤ +1.0 pp.
- A3 (information vs buffer): passes iff UB95[Y(display) - Y(pad_w)] < 0.
  - pad_w shows P0 + k_w·(P0 - t0), and each revision p_i + k_w·(P0 - t0).
  - k_w = Σ(D0 - P0) / Σ(P0 - t0) over all weekday C-30 test riders of window w.
  - k_w is computed from promises only; the script must assert that it reads no alight time.

Claims:
- A1: 'a forecast-aware display removes most anticipable lateness at the measured price'.
- A1 + A2: '... without adding displayed churn'.
- A1 + A2 + A3: '... because of time-of-day information, beyond an equal-price rush-hour buffer'.

Labels and downgrades:
- Every Family A result is labelled 'pre-registered measurement on day-windows previewed by calibration cells'.
- If any leave-one-day-out (drop 14, 15 or 16/11) point ΔY ≥ 0, the label is 'driven by one day'.
- If a stratified cluster-t interval (df = 8 - 3 = 5) has UB ≥ 0, the label is 'fragile to small-cluster inference'.
- The T3.8-style cell bootstrap and the 34-cell deployment mean (weekend Δ = 0 by construction) are co-reported.

FAMILY B (SECONDARY; closed loop)

Setup:
- v1.3 unchanged, K = 2, causal-no15 sources.
- The 16 weekday w07/w08 test cells, 6 day-windows.
- Paired with the reused T3.8 naive runs, valid only if E1 and E2 pass.
- Same stratified cluster bootstrap with 2 strata of 3, B = 10,000, the same seed, 97.5% intervals = indices 124 and 9875.
- Two chains at alpha 0.025 each.

Chain M (classification of Mplus-30F - Mplus-30 forced share, M5_nonNormalShare):
- ARTEFACT iff the relative reduction is ≥ 50%, AND it decreases in 6/6 day-windows, AND UB97.5 < 0.
- PARTIAL iff the relative reduction is ≥ 25% and UB97.5 < 0, but it is not ARTEFACT.
- INCONCLUSIVE iff the relative reduction is ≥ 25% and UB97.5 ≥ 0.
- PERSISTS iff the relative reduction is < 25%.
- Own-break (A > own first promise + 30 s) is classified the same way.

Chain C:
- B-C1 passes iff LB97.5[served(C-30F) - served(C-30)] ≥ -2 riders per cell (the T3.9 margin).
- Deployment rule: recommend integrating the forecast into the Runner only if ALL of:
  - B-C1 passes;
  - visible60(C-30F) ≤ Vis(C-30 display) + 1.0 pp, over the same 16 cells (point);
  - late60(C-30F vs its own first promise) ≤ Y(C-30 display) + 1.0 pp (point).
- Otherwise, recommend the display layer.

Everything else (windows, other arms, the optional tiers) is descriptive, with CIs and no significance language.

predictions.statement: A1 passes. The weekday-21 C-30 display late60 cell-mean is ≤ 1.5% (naive 6.01%), i.e. ΔY ≤ -4.5 pp.
predictions.basis: Day-disjoint task-B, verified read-only by me (unsaved): C-30 LOO-no15 display 7.25% -> 0.00%; causal 13/11 cells 0. Input-only causal r-tables track true weekday-morning growth. Naive weekday baseline 0.0601 from rider-experience-2026-10-05-cells.tsv (verified).

predictions.statement: Weekday-w07 C-30 display late60 is ≤ 3.0% (naive 14.44%), and 14/11 w07 keeps the largest residual of the 3 weekday mornings.
predictions.basis: Input-only: on 14/11 w07 the causal forecast under-predicts growth (bin1 1.057 vs true 1.081; practitioner's 2-h growth 1.514 vs 1.656), while 15/11 and 16/11 are matched or over-forecast.

predictions.statement: Over the 21 cells, early60 rises by ≤ +0.5 pp (point), and by ≤ +1.0 pp in every window.
predictions.basis: Task-B LOO display early60 0.29% (verified). On 16/11 w07 the forecast is above true growth (1.065 vs 1.041), so it slightly over-pads, but by only ~2% of a ~13-min horizon.

predictions.statement: Mean first-drop extension: weekday w07 15-35 s, w08 3-12 s, w17 ≤ 2 s. Mean first-pickup extension in w07 ≤ 10 s.
predictions.basis: Task-B LOO extension 21.2 s (verified). Practitioner's input-only causal-no15 extension: 17.8-19.1 s in w07, 6.2 s in w08, 0.0-0.4 s in w17. Dev pickup extension 5.8 s (unsaved).

predictions.statement: A2 passes, and churn falls: weekday-w07 displayed Vis is ≤ 8% (naive 17.07%), and the weekday-21 ΔVis point estimate is ≤ -2 pp.
predictions.basis: Task-B display visible60 8.78% -> 0.43% (verified). Within-bin invariance of the stretch means display revisions occur only when the Runner's p changes.

predictions.statement: A3 passes. In weekday w07 the per-window equal-price pad leaves late60 at least 2x the display value and at least 2 pp higher.
predictions.basis: Task-B: pad (k≈2.9%) 1.80% vs forecast 0.00% (skeptic/methodologist, unsaved; consistent with my recomputation of the forecast arm).

predictions.statement: Complementarity: the weekday-21 U display late60 stays ≥ 3.0% while C-30 display is ≤ 1.5%, and U display in weekday w17 stays ≥ 5% (naive 6.76%).
predictions.basis: U's w17 lateness is dispatch-caused and the w17 forecast is floored to the naive promise. Task-B U display 7.67% -> 1.50% (verified). U weekday naive 9.72% / w17 6.76% (verified).

predictions.statement: Mechanism: for ≥ 99% of C-30 test riders with dispatch part 0, |A - S_true(t0, P0 - t0)| ≤ 2 s.
predictions.basis: validate-stretch-2026-10-06.txt: 658/658 dispatch-zero dev riders have |residual| ≤ 1.00 s.

predictions.statement: Sensitivity: LOO-no15 and causal-no15 sources differ by ≤ 1.0 pp in weekday-21 C-30 display late60.
predictions.basis: Input-only r-tables: causal and LOO weekday-morning profiles are nearly identical (methodologist: max v1.4 r 1.0766 vs 1.0695 on 14/11 w07).

predictions.statement: Mplus-30F forced share is in [0.10, 0.50] in weekday w07 (naive 0.769) and in [0.05, 0.35] in w08 (naive 0.456). The Chain M verdict is PARTIAL or ARTEFACT (low confidence).
predictions.basis: Naive forced shares verified from analysis-2026-10-02-jobs.tsv. With accurate first promises the +30 s deadline rarely binds. Task-B display proxy: own-break 24.04% -> 0.18-0.52% (unsaved). There is no offline proxy for forcing itself.

predictions.statement: Mplus-30F own-break (A > own first promise + 30 s) in weekday w07 is ≤ 0.15 (naive 0.390).
predictions.basis: Naive M3_shareA_gt_x 0.390 (verified). Dev display proxy as in PB1.

predictions.statement: The closed loop raises churn: over the 16 cells the C-30F visible60 point estimate exceeds naive, and it is higher in ≥ 4 of 6 day-windows.
predictions.basis: Dev v1.3 K=2: visible60 0.080 -> 0.224 and earlier revisions 187.5 -> 1748.1 s (smoke-breakdown-2026-10-06.txt). The static-matrix mechanism is documented in ADDENDUM-2.

predictions.statement: B-C1 passes; the C-30F minus C-30 served difference is in [-2.0, 0] riders per cell (low-medium confidence).
predictions.basis: Dev: served 87 -> 85 (v1.3) and 87 -> 84 (v1.4 D900). Inflated snapshots tighten the 600-s pickup windows and the 1.5x ride cap.

predictions.statement: The deployment rule selects display-only.
predictions.basis: PA5 together with PB3: display churn falls while closed-loop churn rises; same pattern on the dev cell (display 0.023 vs v1.3 0.224).

runPlan:
All runs use v1.3, unchanged, from E:\Code\RideBound-deadline. Outputs go to a new root on C: (e.g. C:\RideBoundData\research\tier3-forecast-v1), using the original T3.8 labels.

Tier 0, gates (3 runs). Run before any test job:
- S1: Mplus-30F smoke on dev d20181112-s10-r1-w07 with the existing forecast-check-k2.json. Implementation check only.
- E1: Mplus-30, forecast off, on one seeded weekday-w08 test cell.
- E2: C-30, K = 1 sham (causal-no15 sources), on one seeded weekday-w07 test cell.
- Halt Family B if E1 or E2 fails. The fallback is then 16 fresh v1.3-off naive runs (C-30 and Mplus-30 x 8 weekday-w07 cells), Family B restricted to w07, and tier 2 dropped.

Tier 1 (16 runs): C-30F and Mplus-30F on the 8 weekday-w07 test cells: 14/11 r3, r4; 15/11 r1, r2, r4; 16/11 r1, r2, r4. Sealed r-table, seeded order.

Tier 2 (16 runs): C-30F and Mplus-30F on the 8 weekday-w08 test cells (same days and samples).

Reserve: ≤ 3 one-time infrastructure reruns.

Committed total: 35 + 3 = 38 new runs, about 3.0 GiB at the measured 77-80 MiB per v1.3 run.

Tier 3, optional (9 runs; only if the live gate allows after tier 2): noise robustness.
- 1 smoke: C-30 naive on dev d20181112-s10-r1-w07 in a measured-base x W4-noise world. Verifies that v1.3 accepts sigma > 0 with a measured base (unverified).
- Then C-30 naive on the 8 weekday-w07 test cells in that world, scored offline by the display layer.

Tier 4, optional (8 runs): C-30 naive, v1.3 forecast-off, on all 8 snow cells (15/11 w14 and w15, r1-r4). Descriptive, with display replay.

Maximum: 55 + 3 = 58 new runs, about 4.6 GiB, plus the 5 dev runs already used (516 MiB measured). That is well inside the ~6,000 MiB headroom over a 51,200 MiB floor on C:. E: is not used unless the owner permits.

Disk gate per job: start only if C: free - 51,200 MiB ≥ 410 MiB, read live with Get-PSDrive. C: read 65,298 MiB now vs ~57,240 MiB this morning, so it is volatile. If the gate fails, stop and list unrun jobs in the sealed order.

Zero-run work:
- display replay on the 170 T3.8 test runs (5 arms x 34 cells);
- display replay on task-B dev (all arms) and the 15 calibration runs (descriptive, flagged);
- pads, factorial, ledger and sensitivities.

Wall time: about 38-58 runs x ~200 s effective at 6 workers ≈ 2.1-3.2 h, on AC power.
implementationChecks: Before the seal, regenerate every dev number cited in the plan from saved, hashed scripts, with output files opened in mode 'x'. This covers: task-B display (C-30, Mplus-30, U; LOO-no15 and causal), pads, extension, visibleD60, the causal-no15 K=2 r-tables for the 6 closed-loop day-windows, and the input-only snow and weekday growth ratios. No forecast outcome may be computed on any test cell before the seal; calibration cells are not recomputed.
Pad comparator code asserts that it reads promises only (no alight times) when computing k_w. k_w values are written to a file before any outcome metric is computed.

Dry-run the full analysis pipeline (Family A and B tables, stratified cluster bootstrap, cluster-t, leave-one-day-out, sign counts) on task-B dev data before the seal. Unit-test the stratified cluster bootstrap on a synthetic case with a known answer.

Equivalence comparator: compares decisions with times, signed v/e/p table, served set, alight times and frames after stripping runId/publicationId(s)/*Hash. Positive control: U vs C-30 on the same cell must differ. Mutation test: perturb one decision time and one alight time; both must be detected. E1 and E2 must pass before any tier-1 job; the halt and fallback rules are sealed.

Per closed-loop run: status pass; v/e/p audit ok; every '[forecast] t=... ratio' line equals the sealed r-table to 1e-6; '[world]' lines identical to the paired T3.8 naive run's; 0 non-normal C-30F decisions. Recompute forced share (M5_nonNormalShare) and own-break with the unchanged t38_analyze.py code, and test_t38.py must pass.

Verify that the v1.3 forecast config JSON for each cell has exactly the causal-no15 sourceDays (14/11: 12,13; 15/11 and 16/11: 12,13,14) and horizonBins 2, and record its SHA-256 in the seal. For E2: horizonBins 1.

For the optional tiers:
- Noise: a new measured-base + W4-noise world config, plus 1 dev smoke confirming v1.3's v1.2 guard accepts sigma > 0 (unverified).
- Snow: confirm v1.3 accepts window starts 50400 and 54000 (WINDOW_STARTS_V1_3 includes them), using the existing grid-snow-v1.json fixtures.
Ledger identity re-check: under display, verify per rider that dispatch + anticipated + unanticipated sums exactly to A - P0, and report any rider where it does not.

Seal: SHA-256 of the plan, predictions, r-tables, configs and analysis-script hashes. Commit and push before the first job, as the binding rules require. Per-job live disk gate and AC-power check; seeded order within tiers.

After results: an independent re-analysis agent works from the raw transcripts, and a number-tracing reviewer checks every reported number against saved outputs, as in T3.8. Then update docs/18 and docs/19 (and the ADR) per AGENTS.md. No repository code changes are planned, so no dotnet test is required; if any repository code changes, dotnet test RideBound.slnx must pass.
